title: Art Programs in Lebanon Bring Beauty to Midst of Crisis
summary: With Lebanon currently being impacted by war, a refugee crisis, and more, stories of beauty can be hard to come across. For ministries active in Lebanon, meeting the spiritual, physical...
summary_zh: 黎巴嫩目前受到战争、难民危机以及更多难民的影响, 对活跃在黎巴嫩的各部来说,满足一个国家的精神、身体和情感需要,只是为了生存而努力,是会付出代价的。 Horizons International的Pierre Houssney说,尽管由于人类在罪恶世界中的堕落,国家仍然面临创伤,但上帝仍然创造了一个充满美丽的世界。 “我认为,美丽对人们的心来说是关于上帝的,特别是当它不仅仅是为了美丽,而是以基督的名义的美丽时。 ”
title_zh: 黎巴嫩的艺术项目将美丽带入危机
content: With Lebanon currently being impacted by war, a refugee crisis, and more, stories of beauty can be hard to come across. For ministries active in Lebanon, meeting the spiritual, physical and emotional needs of a country just trying to survive can take its toll. Horizons International’s Pierre Houssney said that despite the trauma the country faces due to the fallenness of man in a sinful world, God has still created a world that contains beauty. “And I think that beauty speaks to people’s hearts about God, especially when it’s not just beauty, you know, for beauty’s sake, but when it’s beauty in the name of Christ,” Houssney said. “In the midst of the trauma, in the midst of the poverty, we’re trying to give opportunities for believers, who have artistic gifts, to have a prophetic voice through their art to the society, so that we can be calling out for Christ in the midst of the crisis.” Some of these opportunities for creating beauty are fine art classes offered by Horizons International. Horizons International has had up to 35 students at one time participating in these classes revolving around painting or drawing. Students in visual arts classes had the opportunity to participate in an exhibition in Beirut called “His Touch.” People from the community were invited to see the work of beginner students as well as 10 different Christian artists. Graphic design classes offer a more practical element, allowing students to learn a skill they could use in their everyday lives. On the worship side of things, music theory and classes in instruments are helping raise up worship leaders for local churches. One unit teaching guitar, piano, and drums to beginners looking to lead worship at their church had 70 people participate. “And so this new generation needs training, and they need, you know, they need mentoring, and they need to have those skills so that they can, they can lead their congregations in worship,” Houssney said. Though some may have more trouble connecting visual arts directly with ministry, Houssney says social media helps make that connection more clear. Beautiful videos that contain scripture messages alongside visual art tend to get a higher viewership. When posts like that get more views, they can potentially bring more people to Christ. “And so it needs to be beautiful. It needs to be excellent, it needs to be well done. And that’s what our Lord deserves,” Houssney said. “That’s not just what social media deserves.” Currently, Horizons International has to spread resources between humanitarian aid like food and medicine and projects that glorify God through the arts. In the midst of the crisis in Lebanon, pray for God to provide the resources for canvases, studio spaces, art instructors and more. Houssney also says what an organization like Horizons International is here for is to see God open more and more hearts to the Gospel. “So I’m not praying that the church would have less hardship. I’m not praying for you know, for less, you know, political chaos. What I’m praying for is that, through it all, people would continue to open their hearts, and that God will be glorified.” Learn more about the work of Horizons International in Lebanon by visiting https://www.horizonsinternational.org/lebanon-crisis .
content_zh:
黎巴嫩目前受到战争、难民危机以及更多难民的影响, 对活跃在黎巴嫩的各部来说,满足一个国家的精神、身体和情感需要,只是为了生存而努力,是会付出代价的。
Horizons International的Pierre Houssney说,尽管由于人类在罪恶世界中的堕落,国家仍然面临创伤,但上帝仍然创造了一个充满美丽的世界。 “我认为,美丽对人们的心来说是关于上帝的,特别是当它不仅仅是为了美丽,而是以基督的名义的美丽时。”
“在创伤中,在贫困中,我们正试图给有艺术天赋的信徒机会,通过他们的艺术向社会发出预言的声音,以便在危机中呼唤基督。” 其中一些创造美貌的机会是地平线国际提供的精美艺术课.
Horizons International曾经有多达35名学生参加这些围绕绘画或绘画的课. 在贝鲁特举办的名为“他的触摸”的展览。 社区人士应邀观看初学者以及10位不同的基督教艺术家的作品.
图形设计课提供了一个更实用的元素,让学生学习他们日常生活中可以使用的技能. 在事物的崇拜方面,乐器中的音乐理论和课程帮助培养地方教会的崇拜领袖. 一个教吉他,钢琴,和鼓的单位,在他们的教堂里寻找引领崇拜的初学者,有70人参加.
“因此,这新一代需要培训,他们需要,你知道,他们需要指导,他们需要这些技能,以便他们能够领导他们的教会进行礼拜。” 虽然有些人可能更难直接将视觉艺术与部委联系起来,
包含经文信息与视觉艺术的美丽视频往往获得更高的收视率. 当这样的帖子获得更多的观点时,它们有可能将更多的人带到基督身边. “因此,它必须是美丽的。 它需要出色,需要做得好。 这才是我们的主应得的。
“这不仅仅是社交媒体应得的。 目前,地平线国际必须在食品和药品等人道主义援助和通过艺术赞美上帝的项目之间分配资源。 在黎巴嫩危机中,祈求上帝为画布、工作室空间、艺术指导员等提供资源。
霍斯尼还说,象地平线国际这样的组织在这里是为了看到上帝对福音书的开放越来越多. 「所以我不祈祷教会会减少困难。 我不是在为你们祈祷,
我祈祷的是,通过这一切,人们将继续敞开心扉,上帝将受到赞美。” 透过访问https://www.horizonsinternational.org/lebanon-crisis,

title: Abide
summary: This incident took place over 15 years ago, and yet, I remember it clearly. In the buzz of daily life, it is easy to get caught up in the carelessness...
summary_zh: 这一事件发生在15多年前,然而,我清楚地记得。 在日常生活中,很容易陷入清单的粗心大意之中,而忘记遵守他的故意。 我记得我在最后期限之前或晚到之前有多疯狂 以及我对于我们把节目整理好时遇到的所有问题有多沮丧 我将不得不把节目推向全城, 已经七点了 保姆每十分钟给我打电话 然后,我接到一个女士的电话, 她有温柔的克里奥尔口音。
title_zh: v.容忍
content: This incident took place over 15 years ago, and yet, I remember it clearly.  In the buzz of daily life, it is easy to get caught up in the carelessness of the checklists, and forget the intentionality of abiding in Him. I remember how frantic I was once at or late deadline and how frustrated I was at all the problems we were having in getting the program together.  We’d all kinds of equipment failure throughout the day and I was going to have to drive the program across town to get it uploaded to the satellite.  It was already 7 pm and the babysitter was calling me every 10 minutes. Then, I got a call from a lady with a gentle Creole accent. She told me, “I felt led to call you and pray with you.”  I SO didn’t want to talk to this lady, wasn’t interested in being prayed over, and really just wanted to leave to get this program fed and pick my 2-year old up.  I was impatient when I responded to her.  Rather than take insult from what was probably a curt rebuff,  she just said , “Wow. You REALLY need the peace of our heavenly Father on your heart right now.” And…she burst out in song.   Now I’m wondering why I’m on the phone with this crazy lady, and then she prayed through the worship song and then rolled right into praying for me, for my distress, for the things I thought I needed to do…and prayed that I would be still and listen, that my heart would be quiet long enough to remember the awe of God, and that the joy would come back to my heart as we produced MNN… The more she prayed, the more convicted I grew and I realized I was caught up in the ‘do’ and not the ‘be’…and THEN she pulled out the big guns: the story of Mary and Martha. Luke 10:38-42 New International Version (NIV) At the Home of Martha and Mary 38 As Jesus and his disciples were on their way, he came to a village where a woman named Martha opened her home to him. 39 She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to what he said. 40 But Martha was distracted by all the preparations that had to be made. She came to him and asked, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister has left me to do the work by myself? Tell her to help me!” 41 “Martha, Martha,” the Lord answered, “you are worried and upset about many things, 42 but few things are needed—or indeed only one. [ a ] Mary has chosen what is better, and it will not be taken away from her.” She ended our conversation with, “Sometimes, it’s ok to be Mary and sit at the feet of Jesus.  Stuff will still be there to do. It will eventually get done.  But the lasting investment is remembering to sit and BE at the feet of Jesus.” It was a much needed gentle rebuke along with a little encouragement from an unknown sister in Christ that I still remember to this day…thousands of productions later.   What we do is important…but not at the risk of forgetting to abide in Christ.
content_zh:
这一事件发生在15多年前,然而,我清楚地记得。 在日常生活中,很容易陷入清单的粗心大意之中,而忘记遵守他的故意。 我记得我在最后期限之前或晚到之前有多疯狂 以及我对于我们把节目整理好时遇到的所有问题有多沮丧
我将不得不把节目推向全城, 已经七点了 保姆每十分钟给我打电话 然后,我接到一个女士的电话, 她有温柔的克里奥尔口音。
她对我说:我的确被召到你那里来,而且与你一起祈祷。 我本不想和这位女士交谈, 我对她的反应很不耐烦 她没有从可能是一种曲折的反驳中接受侮辱,而是说:“哇。
你现在真的需要我们天父的安宁。” 然后... 她歌声爆出
现在我想为什么我和这位疯狂的女士在电话上, 然后她通过礼拜歌祷告, 然后转而为我祈祷, 为我的苦恼, 为我想我做的事情. 越多她就会
我意识到自己陷入了“做”而不是“做”中, Luke 10:38-42 新国际版本(NIV) 在玛莎和玛丽38的家,由于耶稣和他的门徒们在路上,他来到一个村庄,一个叫玛莎的女人向他打开了她的家.
39 她有一个叫玛丽的妹妹,她坐在主的脚下,听他说的话。 40,但玛莎被所有必须做的准备分散了注意力. 她来到他身边问道,“主啊,你难道不关心我妹妹离开我一个人去工作吗?
" 41 " Martha, Martha, " 主回答说, " 你对许多事情感到忧虑和不安,42件,但需要的东西很少,实际上只有一个。 [a] . . . . . . . . . . 她结束我们的谈话, “有时, 东西会在那里做。 最终会完成的
但是,持久的投资是记住坐在耶稣的脚下。” 这是非常需要的温柔的斥责 加上一个未知的姐妹在基督的鼓励 我至今仍然记得... 我们所做的是重要的... 但不会冒着忘记遵守基督的风险

title: Koinonia
summary: Koinonia (Koy-no-nee’-ah) is a Greek word, occurring 20 times in the Bible, which means “fellowship” or “brotherly love.” It carries with it the meaning of a committed, trustworthy, and dependable...
summary_zh: Koinonia(Koy-no-nee-ah)是一个希腊语词汇,在圣经中出现20次,意思是"fellowship"或"兄弟之爱". 它带有坚定、可信和可靠的关系的意义。 这种关系可以通过参与、分享、给予和贡献来经历。 韩国最早发生的是2:42法案 " 他们致力于使徒的教诲和奖学金、断面包和祈祷。
title_zh: Koinonia
content: Koinonia (Koy-no-nee’-ah) is a Greek word, occurring 20 times in the Bible, which means “fellowship” or “brotherly love.” It carries with it the meaning of a committed, trustworthy, and dependable relationship. Such a relationship can be experienced through participation, sharing, giving, and contributing. The first occurrence of koinonia is Acts 2:42 “They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.” But the rest of the passage reads:  “ 43 Everyone was filled with awe at the many wonders and signs performed by the apostles. 44 All the believers were together and had everything in common. 45 They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. 46 Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, 47 praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.” Christian fellowship is a key aspect of the Christian life. Believers in Christ are to come together in love, faith, and encouragement. The essence of koinonia: “one another”. Scripture commands us to be devoted to one another (Romans 12:10), honor one another (Romans 12:10), live in harmony with one another (Romans 12:16; 1 Peter 3:8), accept one another (Romans 15:7), serve one another in love (Galatians 5:13), be kind and compassionate to one another (Ephesians 4:32), admonish one another (Colossians 3:16), encourage one another (1 Thessalonians 5:11; Hebrews 3:13), spur one another on toward love and good deeds (Hebrews 10:24), offer hospitality (1 Peter 4:9), and love one another (1 Peter 1:22; 1 John 3:11; 3:23; 4:7; 4:11-12). Koinonia is translated many different ways in English Bibles: -fellowship (koinonia), to the breaking of bread and the prayers.” -contribution (koinonia) for them and for all others.” Paul writes to the believers in Philippi: “That I may know him and the power of his resurrection, and may share (koinonia) his sufferings, becoming like him in his death” (Phil 3:10). – Christian living– the dynamic whole of it. It describes an interactive relationship between God and believers who are sharing new life through Christ.  It captures the entirety of this relationship. It involves active participation in Christian community: sharing in spiritual blessings and giving material blessings. How does this idea fit into the theology of ‘And’? Acts 1:8—it empowers us with the chisomo—the grace to DO—the all-inclusive– “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.” And they will know you by your love.  (John 13:35)   “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”
content_zh:

title: Covenant
summary: Isaiah 54:10 Though the mountains be shaken and the hills be removed, yet my unfailing love for you will not be shaken nor my covenant of peace be removed,” says...
summary_zh: 以赛亚54:10 虽然山岳被震动,山丘被移走,但我对你们的爱是不会动摇的,我的和约是不会解除的,"对你们有慈悲的耶和华说: 这些话的音响中有些音乐 在他们下面的思绪,如它横扫着整个创造,把一切分化为短暂和永恒的,凡人和不朽的,仍然比文字的音乐更伟大. `这些'将被删除; `这'将永存。
title_zh: 契  约
content: Isaiah 54:10  Though the mountains be shaken and the hills be removed, yet my unfailing love for you will not be shaken nor my covenant of peace be removed,” says the LORD, who has compassion on you. There is something of music in the very sound of these words. The thought that lies below them, sweeping as it does through the whole creation, and parting all things into the transient and eternal, the mortal and immortal, is still greater than the music of the words. ‘These’ are removed; ‘this’ abides. The thing in God which abides is all-gentle tenderness, that strange love mightier than all the powers of Deity beside, permanent with the permanence of His changeless heart. ‘My loving kindness and the covenant of My peace,’ outlast everything else. The antithesis of what passes and what abides is mind-boggling. ‘all things are in a state of flux’—it’s a basic tenant of physical science…and yet it seems as unchanging as anything we know…it’s the shape of the box…and yet,  if we had nothing abiding beyond this universe, what would be the point? There’s an unspoken  ‘But’  here–  in that vacuum, the Great Spirit moves all the material universe, Himself unmoved, undiminished by creation, or by said vacuum.  The Unknowable whose name means ‘breath’ is YHWH—who comes to us in man-form to help the created move toward and abide in this presence. I’m sort of blown away by how big this passage paints God…and blown away that we are His children…and that we able to abide because of Christ…that our part in glorifying Him and enjoying Him forever comes in walking alongside a global family and telling their stories.  Insignificant, by itself, but being used as a tool to help others abide and recognize the mercy and grace of this big Abba. We can touch the face of God…because He calls us to Himself.

summary_zh: 圣经以弗所书6:10-18(NIV)10 最后,在主和他的强大力量中要坚强. 11,穿上上帝的全盔甲,以便你能够站出来反抗魔鬼的阴谋. 12,因为我们的斗争不是反对血肉,而是反对统治者,反对当局,反对这个黑暗世界的力量,反对天界邪恶的精神力量. 13,因此穿上神的全甲,以便当邪恶之日来临时,你能够站稳脚跟,在做了一切之后,站稳脚跟.
title_zh: Innocent As Doves
content: The Scriptures Ephesians 6:10-18 (NIV) 10 Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. 11 Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes. 12 For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. 13 Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand. 14 Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place, 15 and with your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace. 16 In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one. 17 Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit,which is the word of God. 18 And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people. Matthew 10:16-20 16 “I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves. 17 Be on your guard; you will be handed over to the local councils and be flogged in the synagogues. 18 On my account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.19 But when they arrest you, do not worry about what to say or how to say it. At that time you will be given what to say, 20 for it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.” Today, it’s just been on my mind to bring our attention back to the armor of God and the fact we need to be wise like serpents, innocent as doves. I want to speak to the first part, being wise like serpents. Going to Malta helped bring to my attention how much I don’t know about my own country’s politics, the refugee crisis, trusting God, and even God’s word. I feel like I’m doing “better than the average U.S. citizen.” But, in reality, I don’t know very much. And I’ve realized when it comes to engaging in conversation with others, it’s important to have a handle on topics like these. I.e., talking with my dad about refugees. Having facts and knowing the what the constitution says helps me to better articulate and defend my stance culturally and based by our country’s laws. Knowing about the situation with refugees abroad also helps and is a tool in dispelling the fear which the current administration seems to use to get support to make the calls it’s trying to make both about refugees and immigrants in general. The second part, being innocent like doves…that’s a hard one for me because I’ve thought in the past it means to be naive. I don’t want to be naïve. But being innocent doesn’t mean you’re naïve. I think it means we guard our hearts and take our thoughts captive. What we put into our minds affects the lens through which we see the world and view the Bible—and it has the power to jade us. I.e., rape. I know rape is in the world. I know it is destructive. I’ve seen it damage lives. And I’ve seen God redeem. But, what I don’t need to do is read the part of a book or watch a TV series which details a situation of rape. I don’t need to invite that in my mind to “know” about rape. I’m thinking of a book one of my youth group girls was reading. I haven’t read it, but I see how she struggles with her sexuality, her relationship with God, and for a period even suicide. I also see how her parents are okay with exposing her to things that are a bit mature for her age. Compared to another one of our girls who is aware of what happens in the world, but her parents are careful to protect her from exposure to things which are dark, damaging, fracture her relationship with God. She’s being taught to be innocent, not naïve (or judgmental), and to take her thoughts captive. Both of these girls come from solid Christian homes. I can’t say for sure that what each of these girls has or hasn’t been exposed to has been the big factor in who they are today, but I think it’s clear it has played a role. No barely 12-year-old girl should be reading intimate details about sex or rape. And while I may think not allowing your 12-year-old to watch Harry Potter could be a little excessive, I see how this other young girl is being shaped to cast her thoughts on what is good and to pursue God in all things. Which leads me to the Armor of God. If we are sheep among wolves, if we are God’s people aware of the spiritual battle around us, we need the armor of God. We need our faith, especially when we don’t have answers to why God is still good in hard situations, but know that he is. We need the encouragement of salvation when doubt comes into our minds if we are truly loved by God. We need to know the scriptures, not just where to find them in the Bible, but to really be so in-tuned we can recite them when necessary. We need the breastplate of righteousness because frankly, the world is watching. And with the armor of God and I think it’s important to ask, do we believe in spiritual warfare? Do we believe the world we live in isn’t just made up of cold, hard facts or only what we can see? When I was talking about spiritual warfare with my friend who’s in Ecuador, she mentioned how we leave ourselves open to it. Every morning we can either be aware that it’s there and pray, or we can disregard it and leave ourselves open. Praying against spiritual warfare isn’t just for the days when we can sense it, but even when we don’t suspect it. With all of this said, I want to encourage each of us to really grab hold of the scriptures, of God, and for what it means to put on God’s armor as well as to be wise like serpents, but innocent as doves.
content_zh:
圣经以弗所书6:10-18(NIV)10 最后,在主和他的强大力量中要坚强. 11,穿上上帝的全盔甲,以便你能够站出来反抗魔鬼的阴谋. 12,因为我们的斗争不是反对血肉,而是反对统治者,反对当局,反对这个黑暗世界的力量,反对天界邪恶的精神力量.
13,因此穿上神的全甲,以便当邪恶之日来临时,你能够站稳脚跟,在做了一切之后,站稳脚跟. 14 站稳脚跟,把真理带系在腰上,把正义的胸罩摆好,15 和你的脚固定在和平的福音中。
16,除此之外,还要拿起信仰的盾牌,用这个盾牌可以扑灭邪恶者的所有火箭. 17,拿救世之盔,取灵剑,即神话. 18,并在各种场合以各种祈祷和请求在精神中祈祷. 记住这一点,保持警惕,永远为主的所有人民祈祷。
马修 10: 16-20 16 “我派遣你们同狼群中的羊一样。 因此,要像蛇一样精明,像鸽子一样无辜. 17 个 人 守 着 、 交给 地方 议会 、 在 犹太会堂 被 鞭打
18,就我而言,你们将被带见总督和国王,作为他们和外邦人的见证。 19,但当他们逮捕你时,不要担心该说什么或者怎么说.
在那日,你们得享受你们所应当享受的恩惠,20个不是你们所应当享受的,而是你们父亲的精神。 今天,我正想着让我们重新关注神的盔甲, 以及我们需要像蛇一样的聪明, 我想说第一部分, 像蛇一样聪明。
我对本国政治、难民危机、信任上帝、甚至上帝之言一无所知。 我觉得自己比普通美国公民做得更好。 但事实上, 我意识到,在与其他人对话时,必须处理这类议题。
和我爸谈难民的事 了解事实,了解宪法的内容,有助于我更好地阐明和捍卫我的立场。
了解国外难民情况也有助于消除现政府似乎用来获得支持的恐惧, 第二部分是像鸽子一样无辜, 我不想天真。
但无辜并不意味着你天真。 我认为这意味着我们保护我们的心 并抓住我们的思想。 我们脑海中的东西 影响着我们看到世界和看《圣经》的镜头 并且它有制玉的力量 强奸 我知道强奸在世界上。 我知道这是破坏性的。 我亲眼看到它会伤害生命。 我见过上帝赎罪。
我并不需要读书或看电视连续剧, 我并不需要邀请她去“了解”强奸。 我想到一本我的青年团体女孩读的书。 她的性爱、与上帝的关系, 甚至自杀,
我也明白她的父母 把她暴露在 对她这个年龄来说有点成熟的东西上有什么用 和另外一位我们的女孩相比,她知道世界上发生的事情,但她的父母很小心地保护她免受那些黑暗,有害,断裂她与上帝关系的事情的影响.
她被教导自己是无辜的,而不是天真的(或判断性的),并俘虏她的思想。 这两个女孩都来自坚固的基督教家庭. 我无法肯定每个女孩是否曾接触过她们,
任何12岁的女孩都不应该读到关于性或强奸的亲密细节。 虽然我可能认为不允许你12岁的孩子看《哈利波特》可能有点过分, 但我知道这个年轻女孩是如何被塑造的, 将她的想法投射到什么是好的, 并在万物中追求上帝。 这让我找到神的盔甲
如果我们是狼群中的羊,如果我们是上帝的人民,知道我们周围的精神斗争,我们需要上帝的盔甲。 我们需要我们的信仰, 尤其是当我们没有答案, 如果我们真的受到上帝的爱,我们需要在出现疑问时得到拯救的鼓励。
我们需要知道这些经文, 不仅仅是在圣经中找到它们的地方, 而且为了真正地调和,我们在必要时可以朗诵它们。 我们需要正义的胸罩 因为坦率地说,世界在看着。 我们相信精神战争吗?
我们是否相信我们所生活的世界, 我和在厄瓜多尔的朋友谈论精神战争时, 每天早上,我们要么意识到它的存在,要么祈祷,要么我们无视它,敞开心扉。
祈祷反抗精神战不仅仅是我们感应到的年代, 我想鼓励我们每个人 真正抓住经文,上帝, 以及赋予上帝盔甲的意义,

title: Abraham & Lot
summary: Genesis 13 So Abram left Egypt and traveled north into the Negev, along with his wife and Lot and all that they owned. 2 (Abram was very rich in livestock,...
summary_zh: 创世记13 于是阿布拉姆离开埃及,北上进入内盖夫河,与他的妻子和洛特以及他们拥有的一切一起. 2(阿卜拉姆的家畜,银器,金器非常丰富. 3 从内盖夫出发,他们继续分阶段前往贝瑟尔,在贝瑟尔和艾之间安放帐篷,他们以前在那里扎营。 4,这是阿布拉姆建造祭坛的同一地点,在那里他再次崇拜主.
title_zh: 亚伯拉罕和洛特
content: Genesis 13 So Abram left Egypt and traveled north into the Negev, along with his wife and Lot and all that they owned. 2 (Abram was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold.) 3 From the Negev, they continued traveling by stages toward Bethel, and they pitched their tents between Bethel and Ai, where they had camped before. 4 This was the same place where Abram had built the altar, and there he worshiped the Lord again. 5 Lot, who was traveling with Abram, had also become very wealthy with flocks of sheep and goats, herds of cattle, and many tents. 6 But the land could not support both Abram and Lot with all their flocks and herds living so close together. 7 So disputes broke out between the herdsmen of Abram and Lot. (At that time Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land.) 8 Finally Abram said to Lot, “Let’s not allow this conflict to come between us or our herdsmen. After all, we are close relatives! 9 The whole countryside is open to you. Take your choice of any section of the land you want, and we will separate. If you want the land to the left, then I’ll take the land on the right. If you prefer the land on the right, then I’ll go to the left.” 10 Lot took a long look at the fertile plains of the Jordan Valley in the direction of Zoar. The whole area was well watered everywhere, like the garden of the Lord or the beautiful land of Egypt. (This was before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.) 11 Lot chose for himself the whole Jordan Valley to the east of them. He went there with his flocks and servants and parted company with his uncle Abram. 12 So Abram settled in the land of Canaan, and Lot moved his tents to a place near Sodom and settled among the cities of the plain. 13 But the people of this area were extremely wicked and constantly sinned against the Lord. 14 After Lot had gone, the Lord said to Abram, “Look as far as you can see in every direction—north and south, east and west. 15 I am giving all this land, as far as you can see, to you and your descendants[a] as a permanent possession. 16 And I will give you so many descendants that, like the dust of the earth, they cannot be counted! 17 Go and walk through the land in every direction, for I am giving it to you.” 18 So Abram moved his camp to Hebron and settled near the oak grove belonging to Mamre. There he built another altar to the Lord. At this point in the story, God’s promise to Abraham of the promised land hasn’t come true yet, but good land is part of the promise We’ve seen Abraham have faithful triumphs and failures, but this is a time when Abraham showed great faith once again because there are SEVERAL reasons why Abraham could have taken the better land 1. movement towards God’s promise of good land anyway 2. and this is probably a more striking one to me, but culturally speaking, the older would NEVER defer to the younger. Lot, as the younger, should have deferred to Abraham the older – both in going to him to resolve the disagreement between their herdsmen and in giving him the better pick of land But Abraham wasn’t fixated on culture and on manipulating God’s promises Abraham’s dealings are not in seniority, but in brotherly love and that’s what faith does. Faith resolves tension with generous self-sacrifice Christians often say in tense situations, “Well, I’m not a doormat! I deserve not to be walked all over!” But my pastor said something very striking to me. “Aren’t we glad Christ never said that?” A faithful and generous person doesn’t need to manipulate or control the situation because they are resting in the promises and sovereignty of God Faith leads to trust leads to generosity and self-sacrifice with others.

title: Develop Healthy Tech Habits with Your Teen
summary: ‘Scroll Less, Live More’ helps teens and parents develop the tech skills they need to live a life rooted in reality and steeped in wisdom.
summary_zh: 每个星期天晚上在青年团体,我们通过歌唱进行礼拜的时间之后都会进行简短的布道,然后进行小组讨论。 我带领的高中生们都懂规矩 在打开圣经之前 我们把椅子拉成圆形 然后我们拿出我们的手机,把它们堆在 戒指中间的地板上。 我们不会再碰那些屏幕, 电话堆是一个简单的习惯。 这帮助了我们团体的学生更加关注彼此和圣经文本。
title_zh: 与青少年一起养成健康的科技习惯
content: Each Sunday night at youth group, our time of worship through singing is followed by a short sermon then small-group discussion. The high school kids in the group I lead know the routine. Before we open the Scriptures, we pull our chairs into a circle. Then we take out our phones and stack them in a pile on the floor in the middle of the ring. We won’t touch those screens again until the Bible-study hour is done. The phone stack is a simple habit. But it’s helped the students in our group pay closer attention to both one another and the Bible text. In his practical new book, Scroll Less, Live More: 10 Healthy Tech Habits for Teens , Samuel James commends a number of similar practices. His goal is to give teenagers “a vivid picture of what it looks like to apply [biblical] wisdom to technology usage in today’s digital age” (155). James recognizes that simple, repeatable practices can help young people resist the foolishness today’s tech promotes so they can instead grow in the fear of the Lord. Great Power, Great Responsibility Scroll Less, Live More builds on the foundation James laid in his previous book for adults, Digital Liturgies: Rediscovering Christian Wisdom in an Online Age . One of his main premises is that technology isn’t neutral. Rather, it’s a powerful force that “shapes and influences us in ways we aren’t always aware of” (30). One way tech changes us is by changing our expectations. To illustrate this truth, James points to tech invented in the 19th century: Before the telephone . . . people just accepted that if they weren’t in the same room as somebody, they couldn’t communicate with that person in the moment. After the telephone was introduced, being able to communicate with someone in a different place at any time became not only possible but also important. (125) Similarly, 21st-century tech such as generative AI brings with it both new possibilities and greater expectations: “AI’s capability to produce an amazing variety of work and art with very little direct human involvement creates an expectation that using it regularly for these purposes is normal” (127). The more we off-load our creativity and effort to it, the more we believe we should do so. One way tech changes us is by changing our expectations. Digital technology changes us in other ways too. James draws on the work of tech realists such as Neil Postman , Nicholas Carr , and Marshall McLuhan , but he makes their perspective accessible for adolescents. James repeatedly shows young people how poor digital habits affect their cognition, emotions, and relationships. Living on a phone will slow down thinking, leaving teens feeling anxious, or even angry, amid daily interactions that then become more awkward and strained. Way of Wisdom: Guard Your Heart How do we help young people avoid this path? James gives teens some practical encouragements, telling them to charge their phones somewhere other than in their bedrooms overnight. He also provides a list self-examination questions to help them grow in self-awareness and he appeals to family rules such as only using devices in open areas of the home. But ultimately, James is convinced that using technology well involves more than simply following a list of dos and don’ts. He writes, We don’t need a huge list of rules that will have to be updated every time Apple releases a new phone or a new social media app; we need something that will help us determine how to use technology well in any circumstance. We need wisdom. (16–17) Proverbs says, “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the Holy One is insight” (9:10). James is clear that growing in wisdom and the knowledge of the Lord requires more than adjusting one’s screen-time settings; it takes guarding one’s heart. James encourages teens to think of their hearts as a palace where a king or queen lives. He says, “In any royal palace, you’re sure to find soldiers keeping watch over who and what has access to the very important king or queen inside”; those guards, he contends, are our habits, and “the strength of the soldiers determines how protected the palace is” (158). Early in the book, James calls teens to learn discernment. As he unpacks this habit, he warns them away from the siren song of social media influencers who question parental authority: “When an online influencer who doesn’t know you or care for you speaks about your parents or mentors in a way that makes you want to trust those people less and the influencer more, that’s a massive sign that what you’re listening to is false” (44). Yet James doesn’t merely tell young people to flee digital technology’s dangers; he also beckons them to put on habits that will help them cultivate virtue, in-person friendship, accountability, industrious work, creativity, and rest. For Parents Too Many of these habits are relational. In his introduction, for example, James encourages teens to read his book with a parent, teacher, pastor, or mentor. The discussion questions he includes at the end of each chapter make this counsel practical. This counsel is also wise, because while Scroll Less, Live More is a book for teens, it’s a book for parents too. As a parent and youth worker, I found James’s encouragement to develop a habit of self-awareness convicting. He calls readers to pay attention when being online leads to feelings of anger, anxiety, or boredom so that you know when to “log off and touch grass.” Listless boredom is a form of the sin of acedia : “Spiritual laziness that causes you to fill up on meaningless things so much that you cannot delight in God” (65). He nailed me. How many times do I fill life’s quiet moments—waiting in a line, a few minutes between meetings, or sadly even lulls in conversation—by pulling out my phone instead of being attentive to nature, the people around me, and the Lord? Listless boredom is a form of the sin of acedia . I can get frustrated when I see this tendency in teens, but as Brett McCracken writes , “What parents model with our own devices ultimately matters more than what we say to our kids about them.” James’s book helped me see ways I’ve failed to fight endless scrolling in my own life. As parents, we need God’s Spirit to help us grow in self-awareness about our tech habits. We need his grace to help us confess those failures to the teens we parent and lead. And we need a heart of wisdom and phone-stack intentionality, not just at youth group meetings but throughout our lives. Scroll Less, Live More helps teens and parents develop the tech skills they need to live a life rooted in reality and steeped in wisdom.
content_zh:
每个星期天晚上在青年团体,我们通过歌唱进行礼拜的时间之后都会进行简短的布道,然后进行小组讨论。 我带领的高中生们都懂规矩 在打开圣经之前 我们把椅子拉成圆形 然后我们拿出我们的手机,把它们堆在 戒指中间的地板上。
我们不会再碰那些屏幕, 电话堆是一个简单的习惯。 这帮助了我们团体的学生更加关注彼此和圣经文本。 在他实用的新书"Scroll Less, Live More: 10 Health Tech Habits for Teens"中,塞缪尔·詹姆斯称赞了一些类似的做法.
他的目标是让青少年 " 生动地描绘在当今数字时代将[圣经]智慧应用于技术使用时的情景 " (155)。 詹姆斯认识到简单、可重复的做法可以帮助年轻人抵制当今技术推广的愚蠢,让他们在上帝的恐惧中成长。
Great Power, Great Responsibility Scroll Less, Live More 在他的前书中为成年人奠定的基础基础上, 科技并非中立, 相反,它是一种强大的力量,“以我们并不总是意识到的方式塑造和影响我们”(30)。
技术改变我们的方法之一是改变我们的期望。 为了说明这个真理,詹姆斯指出19世纪发明的技术: 在电话之前, 人们刚刚接受, 如果他们不和某人在同一间屋子里,
在电话引入后,能够随时与另一个地方的某人联系,不仅有可能,而且很重要。
(125) 同样,21世纪的技术,如基因人工智能,带来了新的可能性和更大的期望: " 人工智能在人类很少直接参与的情况下制作各种惊人作品和艺术的能力,使人们期望经常用于这些目的是正常的 " (127)。 我们越是放弃我们的创造力和努力,我们就越相信我们应该这样做。
技术改变我们的方法之一是改变我们的期望。 数字技术也在其他方面改变了我们。 James借鉴了Neil Postman、Nicholas Carr、Marshall McLuhan等科技现实主义者的作品, 詹姆斯一再向年轻人展示,数字化的不良习惯如何影响他们的认知,情感和关系.
生活在电话里会减缓思考, 让青少年感到焦虑甚至愤怒, 智慧之路:守护你的心 我们如何帮助年轻人避免这条道路? 詹姆斯给青少年一些实际的鼓励,让他们在一夜之间在卧室以外的地方充电电话.
他还提供了一份自查问题清单,帮助他们提高自我意识,他呼吁遵守家庭规则,例如只在家庭空旷地区使用装置。 但最终,詹姆斯相信,使用良好的技术不仅仅涉及遵循一个做和不做的清单。
他写道: 我们不需要一连串的规则, 每次苹果公司发布新手机或新社交媒体应用时, 我们需要智慧。 (16-17) 普罗维兹说: " 耶和华的恐惧是智慧的开始,而圣者的知识是洞察力 " (9:10).
詹姆士明白,增长智慧和上帝的知识,不仅需要调整一个人的屏幕时间设置,还需要守护一个人的心脏。 詹姆斯鼓励青少年将自己的心视为国王或女王所居住的宫殿. 他说,“在任何皇家宫殿中,你一定能找到士兵,监视着谁和什么人能够接触到里面非常重要的国王或女王”;
他说,这些警卫是我们的习惯,“士兵的力量决定了宫殿的保护程度”(158)。 在书的早期,詹姆斯召集青少年来学习辨识.
当他解开这种习惯时, 他警告他们远离社交媒体影响者质疑亲权的警笛歌:“当一个不了解你或关心你的网络影响者谈论你的父母或导师时,
但詹姆斯并不只是让年轻人逃离数字技术的危险;他还诱使他们树立习惯,帮助他们培养美德、亲身友谊、责任心、勤奋的工作、创造力和休息。 对于父母来说,这些习惯中有许多是相互关联的。
例如,詹姆斯在介绍中鼓励青少年与父母,老师,牧师,或导师一起阅读他的书. 他在每个章节结尾处包括的讨论问题使这一律师成为实际。 这本书也是明智的, 因为虽然《小说》,
作为父母和青年工作者,我发现詹姆斯鼓励培养一种自我认识定罪的习惯。
他呼吁读者关注网络引发愤怒、焦虑或无聊的情绪, Listless boorom is acedia 罪的一种形式:“精神懒惰导致你充满了无意义的事物,以至于你无法对上帝感到高兴”(65)。 他钉了我
多少次我把手机拔出来, 而不是关注自然、周围的人和主, 无名无姓的无聊是 acedia罪的一种形式。
但正如布莱特·麦克拉肯(Brett McCracken)所写道 , “ 使用我们自己的设备的家长模型最终比我们对孩子说的更重要。 ” 詹姆士的书帮助我了解我如何在自己的生活中与无尽的卷轴斗争。 作为父母,我们需要上帝的精神来帮助我们增强对技术习惯的自我认识。
我们需要他的恩典 来帮助我们承认那些失败 给我们的青少年父母和领导。 我们需要一个智慧的心脏 和电话袋的故意, 不仅在青年小组会议上, 并且我们一生。 Scroll Less, Live More帮助青少年和父母发展他们所需的技术技能,以过着根植于现实和智慧的生活.
author: Jared Kennedy

title: Effective Altruists and the Spreadsheet Gospel
summary: Effective altruism commands us to love our neighbor yet dissolves that neighbor into a statistic. It asks for the fruit of the image of God while denying the root.
summary_zh: 过去十年来,一种新兴的世俗哲学在硅谷扎根. 它现在推动了许多关于政治和技术的对话,特别是因为它的想法决定了我们社会如何对待人工智能。 这种世界观被称作“有效的利他主义”,它正在有一个时刻。 经济学家最近称这个哲学为“本世纪最大的思想 ” , 并称这个运动为“可喜但危险 ” 。
title_zh: 有效的利他主义者和电子表格福音
content: Over the past decade, an emergent secular philosophy has taken root in Silicon Valley. It now drives many conversations around politics and technology, particularly as its ideas shape how our society approaches artificial intelligence. Known as “effective altruism,” this worldview is having a moment. The Economist recently called the philosophy “this century’s biggest idea” and labeled the movement as “admirable, but dangerous.” Even as this philosophy is moving markets and shaping global debates, many Christians are unfamiliar with it. As a Christian and tech-policy analyst based in Washington, DC, where many of these conversations are taking place, I want to explain what effective altruism is, examine what it promises and where it fails to deliver, and show why this budding movement is incongruent with and a poor substitute for the gospel. What Is Effective Altruism? Effective altruism emerged in the late 2000s and early 2010s from the convergence of several intellectual movements, particularly utilitarian philosophy and evidence-based philanthropy. Australian academic Peter Singer provided an important foundation with his 1972 essay “ Famine, Affluence and Morality ,” where he argues that people have a moral obligation to prevent suffering when they can do so at relatively little cost to themselves. At its core, effective altruism is consequentialist, judging the rightness of an action chiefly by its outcomes. The tenets of effective altruism are straightforward: People should use reason, logic, and personal resources to maximize the good they do in society. The Centre for Effective Altruism explains , “We’re committed to prioritizing actions that benefit more lives over actions that benefit a few—that saving a billion lives is more important than saving ten.” The tenets of effective altruism are straightforward: People should use reason, logic, and personal resources to maximize the good they do in society. The movement took shape with the founding of several philanthropic organizations, such as GiveWell and 80,000 Hours . These groups emphasize measuring charitable impact, directing money toward the most effective actions, and choosing “high-impact” careers based on their potential to do good. Their approach to charitable giving has produced endeavors to improve global health , animal welfare , and economic disparities , among other areas. Over the past decade, effective altruism has expanded its scope, focusing on posterity and “longtermism,” the belief that “positively influencing the longterm future is a key moral priority of our time.” The Economist notes a belief this leads to: “Those not born yet should be weighed in the balance—and there could be trillions of them. Many EAs are ‘longtermists’ who feel bound to forestall risks in the distant future, even if that starves today’s good causes, such as helping the desperately poor.” This belief manifests itself in a focus on concerns such as existential risk (e.g., climate change or the next pandemic), nuclear proliferation, and artificial intelligence. For many in Silicon Valley, advanced AI is the defining problem of our day. The concern about a potential AI apocalypse explains why the movement has invested heavily in AI research, AI companies, and AI advocacy and safety. It’s not difficult to see why this philosophy has a natural audience among AI researchers and Silicon Valley tech luminaries. Effective altruism enables technologists to approach ethics in a way that can feel familiar: a series of probabilities, tradeoffs, and expected results—measuring an individual’s moral standing as mathematic calculations, similar to the process of building a software program where different inputs result in varied outputs. For ambitious individuals accustomed to solving complicated projects through ingenuity and critical analysis, this movement delivers reassuring community in an industry that often feels isolating. Adherents have a sense of higher purpose and calling as they’re suddenly confronted with extraordinary individual wealth and wrestle with the consequences of their technological discoveries. It’s hard to describe effective altruism without addressing its more eccentric views, some of which divide the movement itself. For example, the focus on animal welfare has led many in the movement to believe that any and all sentient beings share the same moral value, including but not limited to shrimp . Yes, since a dollar can go a long way to protect the well-being of a single crustacean , this cause could be the most efficient use of charitable giving. Notably, the effective altruist community has also drawn scrutiny for its sexual culture. A 2023 Time investigation highlighted how the movement’s overwhelmingly male membership, heavy overlap between work and home life, and its subculture of polyamory (which some have promoted as more rational than monogamy) has created a “culture of sexual harassment and abuse.” These dynamics have caused many—including Christians—to be concerned about the group’s outsize influence on culture. What Effective Altruism Promises (and Fails to Deliver) Effective altruism’s turn toward longtermism promises that the right people, armed with the right understanding of the stakes, can steer humanity safely through an uncertain future. Many in this community believe their adherence to consequentialism and longtermism gives them a special moral qualification to shape public policy. In their own eyes, effective altruists are the men and women of the hour. This conviction has moved from theory into practice. Political engagement by adherents has increased both on the public stage and backstage through building and funding civil society institutions to influence policymakers to embrace their ideology. One of the movement’s most prominent figures (though he has denied belonging to it), Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, has been leaning on this philosophy to guide his leadership of his company and shape his approach to the future of AI . Yet for all its ambition, the movement struggles to deliver on what it promises. Effective altruism’s confidence in its own reasoning to navigate the future is a hubristic claim to possess unprecedented human knowledge. Any ethic that judges right and wrong by outcomes assumes we can reliably know what our actions will produce. It treats the future as a closed system of causes and effects that the right person or algorithm can calculate. But human knowledge is finite. We can’t trace the full effects of a single choice, much less forecast the welfare of billions of potential lives. At best, an outcome-based ethic can render its moral verdict only in hindsight. Most fundamentally, effective altruism fails us because it’s an ethic without a moral foundation. It has a laudable premise: Too many people around the globe are suffering, and those with means should help. Adherents can accurately quantify certain societal woes and calculate which actions could most efficiently produce the greatest benefit. But the philosophy largely assumes the moral obligations on which those calculations depend. In Singer’s foundational essay, he uses an illustration of a man wearing expensive sneakers who walks past a drowning child. He does a moral calculation that it’s better to save the child even if it ruins his shoes. The illustration works only because we already know the child matters and that walking past would be monstrous. But a strictly consequentialist framework can’t tell us why . If people are ultimately containers of welfare to be added up, then no one has worth in himself. Each matters only as a quantity in a calculation. And who decides which quantities count? Without an external source of moral truth, the answer is ultimately the individual. Each effective altruist must reason his way to his own conclusion about what “the most good” is, and no authority outside himself can tell him he’s wrong. Taken to its logical end, this leaves room for almost anything
content_zh:
过去十年来,一种新兴的世俗哲学在硅谷扎根. 它现在推动了许多关于政治和技术的对话,特别是因为它的想法决定了我们社会如何对待人工智能。 这种世界观被称作“有效的利他主义”,它正在有一个时刻。
经济学家最近称这个哲学为“本世纪最大的思想 ” , 并称这个运动为“可喜但危险 ” 。 即使这种哲学正在推动市场和形成全球辩论,许多基督徒对它并不熟悉。
作为总部设在华盛顿特区的基督教和技术政策分析者,我想解释一下这些对话是何等有效的利他主义,审视它所承诺的以及它未能实现之处,并表明为什么这个萌芽的运动与福音是不一致的,并且是一个糟糕的替代物。 什么是有效的选择?
有效的利他主义在2000年代末和2010年代初从几个知识运动,特别是功利主义哲学和基于证据的慈善运动的趋同中出现.
澳大利亚学者Peter Singer以他1972年的论文“饥荒、富裕和道德”为重要基础,他认为,当人们能够以相对较少的代价来预防痛苦时,他们有道德义务。 有效的利他主义的核心是结果主义,主要根据其结果判断行动是否正确。
有效的利他主义原则是直截了当的:人们应该利用理性、逻辑和个人资源来最大限度地发挥他们在社会中的优势。
有效替代主义中心解释说,“我们致力于优先考虑有利于更多生命的行动,而不是有利于少数人的行动——拯救十亿生命比拯救十亿生命更重要。 ” 有效的利他主义原则是直截了当的:人们应该利用理性、逻辑和个人资源来最大限度地发挥他们在社会中的优势。
这场运动随着多个慈善组织的成立而成形, 这些团体强调衡量慈善影响,将资金用于最有效的行动,并根据他们做好事的潜力选择“影响大”的职业。
他们的慈善捐赠方法 带来了改善全球健康、动物福利和经济差距的努力。
在过去的十年中,有效的利他主义扩大了它的范围,侧重于后代和“长期主义 ” , 认为“积极影响长期的未来是我们时代的关键道德优先事项 ” 。 《经济学家》指出,这导致了一种信念:“那些尚未出生的人应该得到平衡的权衡——而且可能有数万亿。
许多职业介绍所是“长期主义者 ” , 他们认为他们有义务在遥远的将来防范风险, 即使这让今天的好事业饿死, 这种信念表现在关注存在风险(如气候变化或下一个大流行病)、核扩散和人工智能。
对硅谷的许多人来说,先进的AI是我们当今的决定性问题. 对潜在的AI启示录的担忧解释了为什么该运动在AI研究,AI公司,AI宣传与安全方面投入了大量资金. 为何这个哲学在AI研究者和硅谷科技流派中有着自然的读者,
有效的利他主义使技术专家能够以能够感到熟悉的方式处理伦理问题:一系列概率、权衡和预期结果——衡量个人的道德地位作为数学计算,类似于建立软件程序的过程,不同的投入导致不同的产出。
对于那些习惯于通过智慧和批判性分析来解决复杂项目的野心勃勃的个人来说,这一运动在一个常常感到孤立的行业中为社区带来安慰。 坚持者有更高的目标感, 并召唤他们突然面对非凡的个人财富,
很难描述有效的利他主义, 例如,由于注重动物福利,运动中许多人认为,任何和所有神灵都具有同样的道德价值,包括但不限于虾。
是的,由于一美元对保护单一甲壳类动物的福祉可以发挥很大的作用,因此这一事业可能是慈善捐赠的最有效用途。 值得注意的是,有效的利他主义社区也对其性文化进行了审查。
2023年的一次时间调查凸显了该运动绝大多数男性成员、工作和家庭生活之间的严重重叠以及其多元文化(有些人提倡这种文化比一夫一妻制更合理)如何创造了一种“性骚扰和虐待文化”。 这些动态导致包括基督徒在内的许多人担心该团体对文化的影响过大。
有效的利他主义向长期主义的转变会保证,以正确理解利害关系为武装的正确人民能够安全地引导人类渡过不确定的未来。 这个社区中许多人认为,他们坚持后果主义和长期主义,使他们具有制定公共政策的特殊道德资格。
在他们自己的眼里,有效的利他主义者是这个时代的男女. 这种信念已经从理论转变为实践。 通过建立和资助民间社会机构影响决策者接受其意识形态,信徒们在公共舞台和后台的政治参与有所增加。
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei(虽然他否认自己属于这个运动)最知名的人物之一, 然而,运动的雄心壮志却在努力兑现它的承诺。
有效的利他主义相信它自己的通向未来的推理,是一种傲慢地宣称拥有前所未有的人类知识。 根据结果判断对错的任何伦理都假定我们能够可靠地知道我们的行动将产生什么。 它把未来当作一个封闭的因果系统,由正确的人或算法来计算. 但人类的知识是有限的。
我们无法追踪单一选择的全部效果, 充其量,基于结果的伦理只有在事后才能作出道德判断。 最根本的,有效的利他主义使我们失望,因为它是一种没有道德基础的伦理。
它有一个值得称赞的前提:全球有太多的人在受苦,那些有手段的人应该提供帮助。 坚持者可以准确地量化某些社会灾难,并计算哪些行动能够最有效地产生最大的利益。 但哲学基本上承担了这些计算所依赖的道德义务。
在Singer的奠基论文中,他用一个插图说明一名穿昂贵运动鞋的人走过一个溺水的孩子. 他做了一个道德的计算,认为救孩子更好, 插图之所以有效,只是因为我们已经知道儿童的重要性,而且走过去将是可怕的。 但严格地说,
如果人们最终是福利的容器 要加起来, 那么没有人有价值自己。 每种物质在计算中仅作为数量。 谁决定数量是多少? 没有道德真理的外部来源,答案最终是个人.
每一个有效的利他主义者必须解释自己对什么是“最美好”的结论, 顺理成章地说,这为几乎一切留下了空间
author: Nathan Leamer

title: New Free Playlist: 30 Songs of Gratitude to God
summary: Brett McCracken curates a playlist of 30 songs to help you practice gratitude to God—not just on Thanksgiving but every day.
summary_zh: 我越老越相信 感恩姿态是快乐生活的关键 上帝的恩赐是永恒和丰富的——他每天提供的生命和呼吸远远超出我们应有的范围。 提醒人们注意他的慷慨供给, 感恩节之所以如此伟大, 至少要花一天时间去查账, 敬畏真主所赐的恩惠,是人们所关注的。 但感恩节只是一天, 因为真的,我们应该 不断练习感恩。
title_zh: 新的免费播放列表： 30首感谢上帝的歌曲
content: The older I get, the more convinced I am that a posture of gratitude is key to a life of joy. God’s gifts are constant and abundant—his daily provision of life and breath far more than we deserve. Being alert to the constancy of his gracious provision is the epitome of rightly ordered attention . That’s why Thanksgiving is such a great holiday. It’s at least one day dedicated to pausing and taking stock, giving our attention to the Giver of all good gifts. Being alert to the constancy of God’s gracious provision is the epitome of rightly ordered attention. But it’s a shame Thanksgiving is just one day. Because really, we should practice gratitude constantly. What if, as a start, we dedicated the whole month of November to giving thanks? What if we dedicated time each day this month to intentionally naming God’s provision and giving him thanks? To help, I created a new playlist all about giving thanks to God. The playlist has 30 songs (one for each of November’s 30 days) expressing gratitude to God for our salvation in Christ, for the many blessings of marriage and family, and for the beauty of the earth. You can access the playlist now on Spotify and Apple Music . Enjoy! title: The Voice of the Martyrs: Prayers of the Persecuted
summary: We pray for justice, but we do so as forgiven sinners.
summary_zh: “耶和华说,多久? 释放你的愤怒。 . .
title_zh: 殉道者的声音：受迫害者的祈祷
content: “How long, O LORD? . . . Pour out your anger. . . . Let the avenging of the outpoured blood of your servants be known among the nations before our eyes!” (Ps. 79:5–6, 10). As you’re reading through Psalms and you stumble across Psalm 79, you can’t help but wonder what to do with this very Old Testament-sounding prayer. Surely, Asaph needed to be educated in the gospel, right? Revelation 6:9–10 describes the martyrs in heaven who have been slain for their testimony to the gospel and places Psalm 79 on their lips: “O Sovereign Lord, holy and true, how long before you will judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?” Scholars agree the prayer of Psalm 79 is the likely background for the prayer of the martyrs, furthering our appreciation of this as a prayer for the church. It’s a prayer of and for the persecuted church. As we stand alongside them, we have divine warrant to pray Psalm 79 on their behalf. Trevor Laurence explains , “The vengeance petition of Rev. 6:9–10 thus supplies a model for the ongoing prayer of Christ’s body on earth.” Rather than being contrary to New Testament ethics, then, Psalm 79 fuels the church’s longing for every wrong to be made right. Nevertheless, you may still wonder, How do I take up a psalm like this in prayer for my persecuted brothers and sisters without falling into vindictive rage and vengefulness? Thankfully, Psalm 79 provides the guidelines needed to answer this question. Pray in Response to Horrific Injustice Verses 1–4 catalog the horrors God’s people suffered at the hands of the Babylonians who destroyed their temple: They defiled God’s holy place, they gave the flesh of God’s faithful ones to the beasts of the earth, they poured out their blood like water and refused them a proper burial, and they were the cause of God’s people becoming a taunt to their neighbors. Psalm 79 is not prayed in response to petty grievances but birthed out of horrendous evil. Psalm 79 is not prayed in response to petty grievances but birthed out of horrendous evil. This has two implications. First, these prayers do not give license for us to pray such things against just anyone. Second, if we object to such prayers, they challenge us to ask whether we have ever faced anything close to the agonizing evil that gave birth to this prayer. As Jamie Grant posits , “Perhaps our reluctance to appropriate the psalms of enmity is rooted in the comfort of our lives.” If we knew the kind of horror Psalm 79 speaks of (and that our persecuted brothers and sisters endure daily), perhaps we wouldn’t be so quick to dismiss these psalms. Pray for the Glory of God As psalms like this respond to such evil, they are fundamentally concerned with God’s glory. We see this in Psalm 79:6, where the nations’ refusal to call on God’s name is the motive behind Asaph’s cry. Likewise, verse 9 cites the glory of God’s name and his “name’s sake” as a rationale for God to answer this request. And verse 10 is concerned that, at present, the onlooking nations say, “Where is their God?” So Asaph asks that God’s justice would be made known among the nations (v. 10), and that God’s people might praise him for it (v. 13). The glory of God is the ultimate end of the imprecatory psalms. Or as James Hamilton says , “The glory of God in salvation through judgment is the center of the theology of Psalms.” The same is true of imprecatory psalms like Psalm 79. Their controlling desire is “Hallowed be thy name.” Pray with a Humble Posture The imprecatory psalms are not prayed in a spirit of self-righteousness; those praying them understand their need for God’s grace. They pray for justice from a posture of humility, where they confess that this judgment is what they too deserve apart from God’s grace (vv. 8–9). This is not unlike the widow’s prayer for justice in Luke 18:1–8 being paired with the parable of the Pharisee and tax collector in verses 9–14. We pray for justice, but we do so as forgiven sinners. We pray the second petition of the Lord’s Prayer (“Thy kingdom come”) with the fifth petition also in mind (“Forgive us our debts”). Pray with a Desire for Repentance If God could turn his anger away from repentant sinners in exile (Ps. 79:5), then he could do the same for Israel’s enemies. While this is not explicit in Psalm 79, its near neighbor Psalm 83, at the conclusion of this section of Asaph psalms, prays that God would fill the faces of these enemy nations with shame “that they might seek [the LORD’s name]” (v. 16). It is legitimate to see this desire as qualifying the earlier imprecations in the Asaph collection (indeed, in the whole Psalter). Hamilton even suggests every prayer for judgment in the psalms should be read as if containing an implicit “footnote” desiring repentance as a possibility. Pray with the Hope of Final Justice The prayers of judgment, like Psalm 79, are not petty prayers incompatible with a Christian ethic. God’s people pray in response to horrific injustice, aimed at the glory of God, with a posture of humility and openness to their enemies becoming God’s friends. We pray for justice, but we do so as forgiven sinners. The imprecatory psalms, then, fit perfectly with the gospel of Jesus Christ. And they arm the church to intercede for the saints in a day when our Christian brothers and sisters suffer great harm throughout the world. We long for God to answer these prayers through the conversion of our enemies. But if they remain impenitent, it is only right for God to bring justice. And it is thus right for us to pray that he would.

启示录6:9-10描述了在天上的殉道者因对福音的见证而被杀害,并将圣诗79放在嘴唇上: " 神圣和真实的君主啊,你还要多久才能对居住在地上的人判决和复仇? " 学者们同意"诗经79"的祷告是烈士祈祷的可能背景,进一步让我们认识到这是一次祷告.
为教会。 这是受迫害的教会的祈祷。 当我们站在他们一边时,我们有神圣的命令代表他们祈祷诗篇79。 Trevor Laurence解释说,
因此,6:9-10提供一种模式,用于在地球上不断祈祷基督的身体。 Psalm 79并没有违背新约伦理, 反而助长了教会对一切错误的渴望。 尽管如此,你仍然会想,我如何在为我受迫害的兄弟姐妹祈祷时,接受这样的诗歌,而不陷入报复性的愤怒和复仇?
值得庆幸的是,诗篇79提供了回答这个问题所需的准则.
祈求对骇人听闻的不公正行为做出回应, 他们玷污了上帝的圣址,把信主的肉献给大地的野兽,他们把血洒得像水一样,并拒绝给他们安葬,这是真主的宗族变成他们的邻居的恶言。
诗篇79不是针对小不满而祈祷的,而是源于可怕的邪恶。 诗篇79不是针对小的不满而祈祷的,而是源于可怕的邪恶。 这有两个影响。 首先,这些祷告不能让我们允许我们对任何人祈祷这些事情。
第二,如果我们反对这种祷告,他们要求我们问我们是否曾遇到过任何与导致这种祷告的令人痛苦的罪恶相近的事情。
正如Jamie Grant所说 , “ 也许我们不愿接受敌意的诗句, 如果我们知道"诗经79"所说的恐怖(以及我们受迫害的兄弟姐妹每天忍受的恐怖),
祈求上帝的荣耀, 我们从《诗经》79:6中看到这一点。 在那里,各国拒绝呼唤上帝的名声是Asaph哭喊的动机。 同样,第9节引用了上帝的光荣及其 " 名字的缘故 " 作为上帝回应这一要求的理由。
第10节担心的是,目前,目光灿烂的国家说,“他们的上帝在哪里?” 因此,阿萨夫要求将上帝的公义在列国中公之于众(v. 10),并让真主的宗族赞颂他(v.13). 神的荣耀是圣诗的终极结局.
或如詹姆斯·汉密尔顿所说,“通过判断拯救上帝的荣耀是诗歌神学的中心。” 般若菩萨摩诃萨七十九. 他们的欲望是“尊贵的, 以蓬勃姿态祈祷 神圣的诗歌不是本着自以为是的精神祈祷的;祈祷者理解他们对上帝恩惠的需要。
他们以谦卑姿态祈祷正义,他们承认,除了上帝的恩惠之外,这种判决也是他们应得的(vv.8-9)。 这与寡妇在路加福音18:1-8中为正义祈祷, 我们祈祷正义,但我们这样做是宽恕罪人。
我们祈祷主祷告的第二份请愿书(“Thy Kingdom coming”),第五项请愿书也铭记在心(“为我们的债务道歉”)。 如果上帝能把愤怒从流放的悔罪者身上移开(第79:5页),
虽然这在Psalm 79中并不明确,但它的近邻Psalm 83在Asaph psalms这一节结尾祈祷上帝会以耻辱填满这些敌国的脸,"以便他们寻求[耶和华之名]"(v.16). 将这种愿望视为对阿萨夫收藏(事实上,整个Psalter)中早先的杂音加以限定是合理的.
汉密尔顿甚至建议在圣诗中每一次为判断祈祷,都应理解为包含一个隐含的“脚注”,希望能够悔改。 与最终正义的希望一起祈祷 判断的祈祷,如诗篇79,不是与基督教伦理格格不入的微小祈祷.
上帝的人民祈祷,以应对可怕的不公正,以上帝的荣耀为目标,以谦卑和对敌人开放的姿态成为上帝的朋友。 我们祈祷正义,但我们这样做是宽恕罪人。 浸礼诗,那么,完全符合耶稣基督的福音.
他们武装教堂 来替圣徒们说情 在我们的基督徒兄弟姐妹 在世界各地遭受重大伤害的一天里 我们渴望上帝通过改变我们的敌人来回应这些祈祷. 但是如果他们保持无礼,上帝就应该伸张正义。 因此,我们祈祷他会这样做是正确的。

title: Martin Luther in 5 Latin Phrases
summary: Jesus’s perfect life and sacrificial death count for all believers. So God’s righteousness isn’t merely his judgment. It’s also his gift.
summary_zh: 马丁·路德于1483年11月10日出生于德国艾斯莱本. 第二天他在圣彼得和保罗教堂被洗礼. 7岁时,路德进入曼斯菲尔德拉丁学校. 他在那里学习了拉丁语的语法和祷告,并记住了伊索普的寓言。
title_zh: 马丁·路德的5个拉丁短语
content: Martin Luther was born in Eisleben, Germany, on November 10, 1483. He was christened at Saints Peter and Paul Church the next day. At age 7, Luther entered the Mansfeld Latin School. There he learned Latin grammar and prayers, and he memorized Aesop’s Fables . From those early years through his time studying at boarding school in Magdeburg then later at the University of Erfurt, Luther was a diligent student. He kept up with his Latin, and several important Latin phrases appear throughout Luther’s writings. Five of them serve as a good summary of his life and chief theological emphases. 1. Iustitia Dei In July 1505, Luther was caught in a fierce thunderstorm. Panicked and terrified, he bargained with God, promising to become a monk. After entering the monastery, Luther was again overcome by fear. When he led his first mass as a priest, it wasn’t an occasion of joy. Instead, it was filled with trembling. As the service began, Luther took his place at the front of the chapel, and he began to recite the Latin prayers. Luther knew that God is perfect in judgment and completely without sin. So as he thought about iustitia Dei , “the righteousness of God” (Rom. 1:17), terror struck him. Biographer Roland H. Bainton describes the thoughts that plagued Luther’s mind: Who am I that I should . . . raise my hands to the divine Majesty? The angels surround him. At his nod the earth trembles . . . [but] I am dust and ashes. When Luther held up the bread and wine, he shook so badly he almost dropped the cup. During those years growing up in school and at the monastery, Luther only thought of God’s righteousness, or justice, as his active judgment against human sin. He later wrote , Though I lived as a monk without reproach, I felt and knew I was a sinner before God. I had an extremely disturbed conscience. . . . I hated the righteous God who punishes sinners. 2. Extra nos In 1512, Luther became a university professor in Wittenberg. As he studied the Bible for his lectures, he began to see God’s righteousness in a new light. Luther saw how Jesus Christ took on our humanity, how he lived a perfect life and died the painful and shameful death of the cross to take the punishment due for sin. He saw how God raised Jesus from the dead, and how he now justifies Christians by faith. God declares that in his sight, Jesus’s perfect life and sacrificial death count for all believers. So God’s righteousness isn’t merely his judgment. It’s also his gift of salvation. Jesus’s perfect life and sacrificial death count for all believers. So God’s righteousness isn’t merely his judgment. It’s also his gift. What happened when Luther made this discovery? Here’s how he described it: “I felt that I was altogether born again and had entered paradise itself through open gates.” After that day, Luther began to teach that God gives Christians his “alien righteousness,” that is, a righteousness that comes extra nos , “from outside of us.” Our righteousness isn’t from us; it doesn’t come from what we do. It can’t be earned by saying a prayer or even by having a good attitude. Our righteousness is ultimately found in and belongs to another, our Savior Jesus Christ. 3. Crux sola est nostra theologia On October 31, 1517, Luther famously posted his Ninety-five Theses on the door of Castle Church. In it, Luther spoke clearly against the money-raising indulgence schemes Pope Leo X and Germany’s own Prince Albert of Brandenburg had sponsored. The next year, in April 1518, Luther defended these views at the Augustinian order’s spring meeting in Heidelberg. Luther walked to the meeting in fear. He expected the leaders there to sternly rebuke him. After all, that’s what the pope had asked them to do. But to Luther’s surprise, the leaders at the meeting welcomed his defense with excitement. What did Luther say that got his new friends so excited? In his Heidelberg Disputation , Luther described two types of people—the “theologian of glory” and the “theologian of the cross.” Theologians of glory think people are capable and smart enough to know God through human reason. They also say we can know who God’s righteous people are because we see God reward them with political power, success, and wealth. Though Luther didn’t use Albert’s and Leo’s names in his disputation, it’s clear he was talking about their greedy doctrine of indulgences when he described the theologian of glory. Luther’s “theologian of the cross,” by contrast, knows it’s not always people who appear good, beautiful, and powerful by worldly standards who truly know God. After all, Jesus didn’t look glorious on the cross. “One deserves to be called a true theologian,” Luther wrote , “who sees God even in suffering.” As Paul wrote, “God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong” (1 Cor. 1:27). After Heidelberg, the phrase “ Crux sola est nostra theologia ” (“The cross alone is our theology”) became a rallying cry for Luther’s followers. It still is today. 4. Oratio, meditatio, tentatio Luther’s teaching set the Protestant Reformation in motion. In support of his reforms, Luther published hundreds of books, sermons, and hymns. Significantly, he also translated the entire Bible into the language of Germany’s common people. But Luther didn’t want common people to merely read Scripture. He wanted them to study it too. In the 1539 preface to the Wittenberg edition of his German writings, Luther wrote, “God himself lives in the Bible. Therefore, worthy Christian: get in, get in!” Luther gave his readers three rules for digging into God’s Word. Each has its own Latin term: prayer ( oratio ), meditation ( meditatio ), and suffering ( tentatio ). A ‘theologian of the cross’ knows it’s not always people who appear good, beautiful, and powerful by worldly standards who truly know God. The first rule is kept before we read the Bible. Luther wrote, “Kneel down in your private room and with humility, pray to God to give you his Holy Spirit to enlighten and guide and give you understanding.” The second rule is kept while reading: “Read and reread the very words written down in the Bible. Observe and think about what the Holy Spirit means.” The last rule is kept when we practice what the Scriptures say. Luther said, As soon as you begin to know God’s word, the devil will afflict you. . . . This suffering will teach you how right, true, sweet, lovely, mighty, and comforting God’s word is. It is wisdom supreme. 5. Simul iustus et peccator Luther was zealous and driven. He once said, “When I want to compose, write, pray, and preach well, I must be angry.” But while anger may have given Luther energy for work, it too often burned out of control. Sadly, today, Luther is as famous for his harsh words spoken against his enemies and the Jews as he is for recovering the biblical doctrine of justification. Throughout his life, Luther taught that believers are simul iustus et peccator . That’s Latin for “simultaneously justified and a sinner.” Both realities are true of every Christian. Both were true of Luther. He was a broken man who desperately needed God’s grace, and he knew it. Luther died while visiting Eisleben on February 18, 1546. Before he died, Luther scribbled out his last written words: “We are beggars. This is true.” Luther knew he could never earn God’s grace. Salvation isn’t won through indulgences or daily prayers. This is what Luther had discovered from the Bible and taught again to the world. God sent his only Son. Christ has overcome the world. All he asks of poor, begging sinners is that we believe.

马丁·路德于1483年11月10日出生于德国艾斯莱本. 第二天他在圣彼得和保罗教堂被洗礼. 7岁时,路德进入曼斯菲尔德拉丁学校. 他在那里学习了拉丁语的语法和祷告,并记住了伊索普的寓言。
从早年到后来在马格德堡的寄宿学校学习,路德是一名勤奋的学生。 他跟上他的拉丁语,几个重要的拉丁语短语出现在路德的著作中. 其中五篇很好地总结了他的生活和主要神学重点. 一、导 言
1505年7月,路德遭遇猛烈的雷暴. 惊慌惊恐,他与神讨价还价,许诺成为和尚. 进入修道院后,路德再次被恐惧所克服. 当他第一次作为牧师主持弥撒时, 相反,充满了颤抖。
随着礼拜的开始,路德在礼拜堂的前面取代了他的位置,他开始背诵拉丁语祈祷. 路德知道上帝在判断上是完美的,并且完全没有罪恶. 因此,当他想到“上帝的义”iustitia Dei(1:17)时,恐怖袭击了他。 传记家罗兰·H·班顿(Roland H. Bainton)描述了困扰路德的思想:我应该是谁?
向神圣的陛下举手? 众天神围绕他. 在他点头的时候,大地会颤抖... 当路德拿起面包和葡萄酒时,他摇得那么厉害,差点把杯子掉了. 在那些在学校和修道院长大的年头里,路德只把上帝的正义或正义视为他对人类罪恶的积极判断。
他后来写道, 虽然我作为一个和尚生活 没有责备, 我感到和知道我是上帝面前的罪人。 我有一个极度不安的良心。 我恨那些惩罚罪人的善良上帝 2. 1512年,路德成为维滕贝格大学教授。 当他为自己的讲座学习圣经时,他开始在新的光芒中看到上帝的正义.
路德看到耶稣基督如何对待我们的人性,他如何过上完美的生活,并死于十字架的痛苦和可耻的死亡,以承担罪责的惩罚. 他看见了上帝如何使耶稣从死里复活,以及他现在如何以信仰为基督徒辩护. 上帝宣布,在他看来,耶稣的完美生活和牺牲的死亡对所有信徒都很重要。
因此,上帝的正义不仅仅是他的判断。 这也是他的救赎天赋。 耶稣的完美生活和牺牲的死亡是所有信徒的计数. 因此,上帝的正义不仅仅是他的判断。 也是他的天赋。 当路德做出这个发现时发生了什么?
他这样描述 : “ 我感到我再次出生,并通过开放的大门进入天堂。 ” 这天之后,路德开始教导上帝给予基督徒“外星人的正义 ” , 即“来自我们以外的”一种格外不义的正义。 我们的正义不是来自我们,
祈祷, 我们的正义最终被发现 并属于另一个,我们的救主耶稣基督。 3. Crux sola est nostra Godologia 1517年10月31日,路德在城堡教堂的门上贴出了他的95本论文。
在其中,路德明确反对教皇利奥十世和德国自己的勃兰登堡阿尔伯特亲王赞助的集资宽恕计划。 次年,1518年4月,路德在海德堡举行的奥古斯丁命令春季会议上为这些观点辩护. 路德在恐惧中走进会议. 他希望那里的领导人严厉斥责他。
这毕竟是教皇要求他们做的。 但令路德惊讶的是,与会领导人激动地欢迎他的辩护. 路德怎么说 他的新朋友这么兴奋?
路德在海德堡争论中描述了两类人——“荣耀神学家”和“十字架神学家”。 荣耀的神学家认为人们有能力和聪明,足以通过人类理性来认识上帝. 他们又说,我们可以知道上帝的善良人民是谁,因为我们看到上帝以政治力量、成功和财富奖励他们。
虽然路德在争论中并没有使用艾伯特和李奥的名字,但很明显,当他描述荣耀神学家时,他在谈论他们贪婪的宽恕理论。 相对而言,路德的“十字架神学家”知道,并非总能以世界标准看好、美丽和强大的人真正了解上帝。 毕竟耶稣在十字架上并不光荣。
路德写道 : “ 一个人应该被称为真正的神学家。 ” 正如保罗所写的那样,“上帝选择世界上愚蠢的事物来羞辱智者;上帝选择世界上软弱的事物来羞辱强者”(《法典》第1:27条)。 在海德堡之后,“Crux sola est nostra Godologia”这一短语成为路德追随者的呼声。
今天还是这样。 4. Oratio、meditatio、tentatio Luther的教学使新教改革运动开始。 为了支持他的改革,路德出版了数百本书,布道,还有赞美诗. 重要的是,他还将整个圣经翻译成德国普通人的语言. 但路德并不想普通民众只读圣经。 他想让他们也学习它。
路德在他的德国著作维滕贝格版的1539年序言中写道:"上帝自己生活在圣经中. 因此,值得的基督徒:上车,上车!” 路德给读者三条规则, 他们都有自己的拉丁语词汇:祷告(oratio),冥想(meditatio),痛苦(tentatio).
一个“十字架的神学家”知道,并非总能以世界标准显示良好、美丽和强大的人真正了解上帝。 第一条规则在我们读圣经之前就被保留.
路德写道:“在你的私人房间里恭敬地跪下,祈祷真主赐予你他的圣灵以启蒙、引导和谅解。” 第二条规则在读本时保留:“读和重读圣经中写下的文字。 观察和思考圣灵的意义。” 最后一个规则是当我们实践圣经里所说的时,
路德说:一旦你听到上帝的话,恶魔就会折磨你。 这种痛苦将教你如何正确、真实、甜蜜、可爱、强大和安慰上帝的话。 这是智慧至高无上的。 5. Simul iustus et peccator Luther是热心的,受到驱使。
他曾经说过,“当我想写作、写作、祈祷和讲道的时候,我一定生气。” 虽然愤怒可能让路德精力充沛地工作,但经常被烧得失控. 可悲的是,今天,路德以其对敌人和犹太人的严酷言辞而闻名,如同他收复圣经的辩解学说一样.
路德在一生中教诲信徒们, 这是拉丁语的“极端合理和罪人 ” 。 每个基督教徒都是这样 路德也一样 他是一个破碎的人,迫切需要上帝的恩惠,他知道这一点。 1546年2月18日路德在访问艾斯莱本时去世.
在他死前,路德写了最后的文字:“我们是乞丐。 这是事实。” 路德知道自己永远得不到上帝的恩惠。 救世主不是通过宽恕或日常祈祷赢得的。 这是路德从圣经中发现的,并且再次向世界传授. 上帝派他唯一的儿子 基督战胜了这个世界 他只要求穷人,乞讨罪人 是我们相信的。

title: ‘Mosquito Bowl’: Football Stars on the Front Lines
summary: Peter Berg’s ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ is essentially ‘Friday Night Lights’ meets ‘Hacksaw Ridge.’
summary_zh: Peter Berg's The Mosquito Bowl本质上是周五夜灯, 这部电影具有与星期五夜光相同的创意氛围(gritty手持相机、哑调色板、天空后摇滚音轨爆炸), 也像伯格的星期五夜光一样, 《蚊子碗》(现在在剧院里; 2022年的一本书——副标题是《二战中的生死游戏》——只有一章(41章)专门讲述1944年的足球赛事,被誉为“蚊子碗”。 这本书大多是关于战争的,而留下妻子,孩子的年轻人,以及有前途的NFL事业来与之战斗.
title_zh: “蚊子碗” ：前线的足球明星
content: Peter Berg’s The Mosquito Bowl is essentially Friday Night Lights meets Hacksaw Ridge . It’s a movie with the same creative vibe as Friday Night Lights (gritty handheld camera, muted color palette, Explosions in the Sky post-rock soundtrack) but applied to a brutally violent true story of WWII’s Battle of Okinawa, one of the single bloodiest battles of the 20th century. Also like Berg’s Friday Night Lights , The Mosquito Bowl ( out now in theaters ; coming to Netflix November 25) is based on a book by Pulitzer Prize–winning journalist Buzz Bissinger . The 2022 book—subtitled A Game of Life and Death in World War II —only has one chapter (of 41) devoted to the actual 1944 football game dubbed “The Mosquito Bowl.” Most of the book is about the war, and the young men who left wives, kids, and promising NFL careers to fight it. Likewise, Berg’s film adaptation is mostly a somber, unflinching WWII film, with a brief reprieve of joy in the form of a football game on Guadalcanal between the 4th and 29th regiments of the 6th Marine Division. Just as in Friday Night Lights , where the drama of high school football parallels the struggles and triumphs of life off the field, the football game in The Mosquito Bowl parallels the “game of life and death” that surrounds the men at war. Sports are interesting in this way: They provide escape from real life but also training for it, an arena of danger and high stakes but not ultimate stakes. Sports often map onto life—we draw up plans and plays but have to improvise; we get hurt but can heal; we thrive individually through teamwork; sometimes we win and sometimes we lose. Yet sports are unlike real life too. Winning or losing on the field is a matter of trophies and glory, but off the field, it can be a matter of life and death. Young Men Willing to Fight and Die The Mosquito Bowl (rated R for graphic war violence and language), opens with a well-known epigraph from Herbert Hoover : Older men declare war. But it is youth that must fight and die. And it is youth who must inherit the tribulation, the sorrow, and the triumphs that are the aftermath of war. This is a movie about youth—or rather, the passage from youth into adulthood that war accelerates. This is a movie about youth—or rather, the passage from youth into adulthood that war accelerates. The movie opens with muddy college football scenes in the fall of 1941, as the four central characters are introduced: John McLaughry (Nicholas Galitzine), Brown quarterback; Bob Baumann (Bill Skarsgård), University of Wisconsin tackle; Tony Butkovich (Ray Nicholson), Purdue fullback; and Dave Schreiner (Tom Francis), Wisconsin end. They were all-star athletes with promising futures. Many of them were collegiate All-Americans and drafted by NFL teams. Yet December 7, 1941, happened, and their futures were all changed. Once bound together by football skill, friendly rivalry, and fierce competition on the gridiron, these men soon bonded in a different setting: as marines in WWII’s savage Pacific theater. Instead of fighting for yards on the field, they fought for ground in a war of attrition on Okinawa. Instead of a football in hand, they carried guns and bayonets. Instead of tackling their opponents, they wrestled them to the death in hand-to-hand combat. Like many in the Greatest Generation, these men volunteered to enlist and fight. The Mosquito Bowl celebrates their duty and sacrifice. In one scene, Baumann’s younger brother says, “You don’t have to go,” to which Baumann replies, “I do. I’m needed.” It’s hard to imagine star athletes, whether collegiate or professional, volunteering to go to war in 2026. But in 1943, it was normal. Okinawa, Bissinger writes in the book, was “by far the largest collection of athletes ever to die in a single battle.” And in the entirety of WWII, 21 NFL players died in combat, as well as two players from Major League Baseball. Why were they so willing to lay down their lives? Perhaps back then, men had the bigger horizon more in view. Life isn’t about serving oneself. It’s about serving others, fighting for things bigger than personal fulfillment. As Dave Schreiner tells John McLaughry, “This is us sacrificing for the unborn. What other real thing is there? What’s the point in all of this if it’s not for passing something on?” Numbed by War-Movie Violence The Mosquito Bowl honors the Greatest Generation and is commendable in its straightforward embrace of manly virtues like duty and sacrifice. But I disliked several aspects of the film. One is the language. I realize wartime soldiers in every era tend to be prolific in their employment of profane language. But even if men in the 1940s were as creative with the f-word as they are in this movie, is it really essential to the movie? It makes the film much less likely to be watched by families, which is a shame because it’s the sort of thing dads might want to watch with their younger sons. I also wish Berg had given less screen time to bloody battles and more time to quieter character moments and the titular football game. I get that it’s important to underscore the savage bloodbath that was the Pacific theater, and I get that the joyful escape of football is most pronounced when juxtaposed with the horrific realities of war. But it’s hard for contemporary war movies to viscerally depict the “war is hell” experience after the genre has been so saturated. Edward Berger’s adaptation of All Quiet on the Western Front (2022) felt like the final word on war-movie blood and guts. We’ve become numb to watching bodies get mangled every which way. Going forward, movies about savage warfare probably need to take a different approach. There are ways to capture battle horror without showing every gruesome detail. Furthermore, the desaturated, shaky-camera, chaotic choreography of war movies has become clichéd. I checked out a bit during these prolonged battle scenes. At times, it felt like Berg was inspired by Terrence Malick’s Guadalcanal movie, The Thin Red Line (one of the best war movies of all time). But what made Malick’s film so effective is that it employed violence only in a few intense, lyrical sequences, juxtaposed with long stretches of more contemplative material and tender character moments. The experience of war is important to capture accurately. But a war film becomes great when the meaning of war is also a focal point. Clint Eastwood’s WWII diptych, Flags of our Fathers and Letters from Iwo Jima (2006), strikes this balance well. The action-to-reflection ratio is not quite right in The Mosquito Bowl . Football as Far as the Curse Is Found The high point of Berg’s movie is the Mosquito Bowl game, even though it occupies too little of the overall runtime. In a movie that is rather bleak thematically and visually, the game provides a much-needed moment of joy for the characters and audience. Hosted as a morale booster for soldiers who would soon be sent to fight on Okinawa, the game (broadcast on the “mosquito radio network”) was set up to be “two-hand touch” only but quickly devolved into full-on tackle. Some of the guys wore Santa hats. There were big smiles, laughs, playful rivalry: young men allowed to be boys again. Here’s how Bissinger describes it in the prologue of his book: For roughly two hours the Mosquito Bowl wasn’t simply a reminder of what life had once been like for the players, but freedom and abandon, with the spectators captured in the same moment, screaming their heads off, whether drunk or sober. The beauty of sports, the ultimate power of it to carry you away, had never been stronger. But the scene is also bittersweet, for we know it’s not reality. Real life is harsh. Okinawa looms. Many of these boys playing football on Christmas Eve 1944 won’t live to see Christmas Eve 1945. This scene reminded me of the resonant poetry of Friday Night Lights , which depicted football in much the same way: youthful vibrancy and freewheeling joy, but tempered by the painful pressures
